messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary deploy r-2026.03.17-42 (model-serving) reporting p95 latency jump and elevated errors. p95 120ms -> 1.4s, error_rate 4.2%. link: https://infra.internal/deploys/2026-03-17-42/logs and graphs: https://metrics.internal/r/model-serving/canary

alice: paging oncall SRE. I’m on it, will triage. can someone confirm if automated rollback fired?

deploy-bot: Automated rollback DID NOT trigger: threshold config 'canary_auto_rb' set to 10% error but current error_rate evaluates to 4.2% (latency spike only). No auto-unwind.
bob: I’m release-eng, looking. if we can flip the canary flag quickly we can stop routing traffic. flag: `model_v2_canary` set to `false`. I’ll prepare drain commands.

carol: product — any user-facing 500s or manifests of customer impact? need to know whether to page CS.

frank: from logs: a couple of streaming timeouts observed, ~5 live sessions max, a handful of increased 502s from proxy (not full 500 surge). latency seems correlated with sequence-length > 2048 requests.

eve: CS: i’ll stand by. if you confirm a customer list i’ll notify top-3 SLA accounts.

dave: support here — opening S2 for affected accounts. ticket IDs: S2-11287, S2-11288.

bob: executing flag flip now -> `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/flip -d '{"flag":"model_v2_canary","value":false}'`

bob: :gear: command output: `{
  "flag":"model_v2_canary",
  "old":true,
  "new":false,
  "changed_by":"bob"
}`

bob: draining canary pods:```kubectl -n model-serving label pod -l canary=true traffic=drain; kubectl patch deploy model-serving-canary -p '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'```

bob: drain started, pods terminating (3 -> 0). routing layer will shift to stable variant within ~30s.

alice: automate smoke checks after roll-back applied. checklist: 1) /health (200) 2) p95 < 300ms on synthetic suite for seq_len 512/1024 3) no errors > 1% 4) sanity chat prompt correctness sample.

bob: smoke curl: `curl -sS https://api.internal/model/health` -> `{"status":"ok","version":"r-2026.03.17-41"}`

bob: synthetic run results (quick): seq512 p95=130ms, seq1024 p95=210ms, error_rate=0.3% — trending back to normal.

frank: metrics: p95 now 180ms, error_rate 0.4%. requests routed off canary.

carol: customer impact: eve, contact top-3 and mention temporary latency/timeouts, mitigation performed, offering follow-up postmortem. :telephone_receiver:

eve: contacting customers now. I’ll post responses.

dave: noted — customers S2 opened and linked to incident.

alice: root-cause hypothesis for SRE: mis-compiled kernel path for long sequences in r-2026.03.17-42 that causes GC/CPU contention under certain batch shapes. we should hold rollout until QA validates fix.
bob: agree. will pin stable image r-2026.03.17-41 as default and block subsequent auto-rollouts for the model-serving job.

bob: commands run: `kubectl set image deploy/model-serving model-container=registry/redwood/model:r-2026.03.17-41` and `flux suspend kustomization/model-serving-canary` to prevent reapply.

alice: verification steps completed: smoke health ✅, synthetic latency ✅, error rate ✅. leaving in safe state for 30m to ensure no regression.

carol: assign postmortem to bob+alice+frank. include: what changed in build, kernel selection logic, and flag gating for seq>1024. target writeup EOD.

eve: sent customer messages: 3 customers notified, response queued for follow-up.

frank: creating a short alert rule to catch p95 spikes separate from error thresholds so auto-rollback will consider both latency and errors going forward.

bob: thanks all. closing active mitigation. will handover to change-review for new rollout plan. :white_check_mark:

alice: oncall note: if latency spikes reappear after 30m, page `#eng-sre oncall` and escalate to infra-eng.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT LOGGED: incident-2026-0317-42-canary-latency — responders: alice, bob, frank. followups: postmortem and flag gating.
